html:
A rising of the Greek cities of Ionia, on the west coast of Anatolia, against Persian rule from 499 to 493 BCE. It was the opening act of the Greco Persian Wars.

It was started by Aristagoras, the ruler of Miletus, after a failed expedition he had led for the Persians. The cities threw out their Persian backed tyrants. Athens sent twenty ships and Eretria five, and in 498 BCE the rebels burned Sardis, the Persian regional capital. The revolt spread to Cyprus and Caria.

Persia struck back. In 494 BCE its fleet crushed the Ionians at the Battle of Lade, and Miletus was sacked and many of its people deported. When an Athenian playwright staged a tragedy about the fall of Miletus, the audience wept and he was fined. Darius now wanted to punish Athens and Eretria, which led to the expedition that ended at the Battle of Marathon in 490 BCE. Herodotus is the main source.
sum: A rising of the Greek cities of Ionia, on the west coast of Anatolia, against Persian rule from 499 to 493 BCE. It was the opening act of the Greco Persian Wars.
